overview: Black waits with 2...c6, a flexible move that can become a Slav (...d5), a Czech Benoni (...e5), or a King's Indian or Queen's Indian set-up. White can play for the usual centre with c4 or e3 and Bf4. The game is flexible and positional, with no forcing lines. I know this only as a transposing move order.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with c4, Nc3 or e3 and Bf4 or g3
Take a space edge in the centre
Choose a favourite set-up against the c6 pawn

black_ideas.idea: Aim for a Slav-style set-up with ...d5
Choose ...g6 or ...e6 depending on White's set-up

typical_structures.structure: Possible Czech Benoni or KID structures after ...e5 or ...g6

character.notes: Solid and flexible for Black; it is hard to attack.

approach.notes: Played rarely by strong players but not an oddity.

level.notes: Choosing the right set-up is the hard part.

character.reason: A waiting move leading to a Slav-style shell.
